\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بچھڑنا} (bichhaṛnā)}{بچھڑنا (bichhaṛnā)}]{\ur{بچھڑنا} (bichhaṛnā) — to be separated}

\label{lesson:UR-C298-bichharna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for refuge, then the Urdu for affected.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بچھڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بچھڑنا}} — \emph{bichhaṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be separated\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میلے} \ur{میں} \ur{بچہ} \ur{ماں} \ur{سے} \ur{بچھڑ} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mele meṅ bachchā māṅ se bichhaṛ gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the fair the child got separated from his mother.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بچھڑ} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh bichhaṛ gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بچھڑنا}} (\emph{bichhaṛnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bichuṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}is separated\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 11651). The person you lose takes \textbf{\ur{سے}}: \textbf{\ur{ماں} \ur{سے} \ur{بچھڑ} \ur{گیا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bichhaṛnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bichhaṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mele meṅ bachchā māṅ se bichhaṛ gayā.} — At the fair the child got separated from his mother.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for refuge, then the Urdu for affected, then say \emph{bichhaṛnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بچھڑنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be separated\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بھٹکنا} (bhaṭaknā)}{بھٹکنا (bhaṭaknā)}]{\ur{بھٹکنا} (bhaṭaknā) — to wander; to lose one's way}

\label{lesson:UR-C298-bhatakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for affected, then the Urdu for to be separated.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بھٹکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بھٹکنا}} — \emph{bhaṭaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to wander; to lose one's way\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{رات} \ur{بھر} \ur{جنگل} \ur{میں} \ur{بھٹکا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh rāt bhar jangal meṅ bhaṭkā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بھٹکی}, \emph{voh bhaṭkī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بھٹکنا}} (\emph{bhaṭaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bhaṭaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to wander\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{bhraṣṭá}, \textquotedblleft{}fallen\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9655).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گمشدہ} (gumshudā)}{گمشدہ (gumshudā)}]{\ur{گمشدہ} (gumshudā) — missing; lost}

\label{lesson:UR-C298-gumshuda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be separated, then the Urdu for to lose one's way.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گمشدہ}}
\textbf{\ur{گمشدہ}} — \emph{gumshudā} — \textquotedblleft{}missing; lost\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{گمشدہ} \ur{بچہ} \ur{صبح} \ur{مل} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gumshudā bachchā subah mil gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The missing child was found in the morning.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گمشدہ}} (\emph{gumshudā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{gum-shuda}, built from \emph{gum}, \textquotedblleft{}lost\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{shuda}, \textquotedblleft{}become\textquotedblright{}. It is the word on notices for missing people.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gumshudā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gumshudā bachchā subah mil gayā.} — The missing child was found in the morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to be separated, then the Urdu for to lose one's way, then say \emph{gumshudā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تسلی} (tasallī)}{تسلی (tasallī)}]{\ur{تسلی} (tasallī) — comfort; reassurance}

\label{lesson:UR-C298-tasalli}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to lose one's way, then the Urdu for missing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تسلی}}
\textbf{\ur{تسلی}} — \emph{tasallī} — \textquotedblleft{}comfort; reassurance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{کو} \ur{پولیس} \ur{سے} \ur{تسلی} \ur{ملی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ ko polīs se tasallī milī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police reassured the mother.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تسلی}} (\emph{tasallī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tasallī}, \textquotedblleft{}consolation\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{تسلی} \ur{دینا}} is to comfort someone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ملاپ} (milāp)}{ملاپ (milāp)}]{\ur{ملاپ} (milāp) — a reunion; a coming together}

\label{lesson:UR-C298-milap}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for missing, then the Urdu for reassurance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ملاپ}}
\textbf{\ur{ملاپ}} — \emph{milāp} — \textquotedblleft{}a reunion; a coming together\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شام} \ur{کو} \ur{ماں} \ur{بیٹے} \ur{کا} \ur{ملاپ} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shām ko māṅ beṭe kā milāp huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the evening mother and son were reunited.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ملاپ}} (\emph{milāp}) is built on \textbf{\ur{ملنا}}, to meet, which CDIAL lists for Hindi under Sanskrit \emph{miláti}, \textquotedblleft{}meets\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10133): a meeting again after a parting.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
